subject: Biology
title: Plankton: The Ocean's Foundation
description: A micro-lesson that makes Plankton: The Ocean's Foundation usable.

hook.text: Plankton are invisible to the naked eye, but they support every food chain in the ocean.

buildup.text: Phytoplankton photosynthesize like plants. Zooplankton are tiny animals that eat phytoplankton.

discovery.text: A single liter of seawater can contain millions of phytoplankton cells.

twist.text: When phytoplankton die, they sink and carry carbon to the deep ocean—a process called the biological pump.

climax.text: Without plankton, there would be no fish, no whales, no coral reefs, and far less oxygen.

punchline.text: The smallest creatures run the biggest system.

quiz.question: What is the biological pump?
options: Dead plankton sinking and carrying carbon to the deep ocean
Whales pushing water to the surface

details.summary: Plankton are drifting organisms that form the base of nearly all marine food webs. Phytoplankton produce about half of Earth's oxygen through photosynthesis, while zooplankton transfer this energy to larger animals. Together they support almost all ocean life from anchovies to whales.
details.whyItMatters: Plankton produce half the oxygen we breathe and absorb enormous amounts of CO2. Declining plankton populations due to warming and acidification could disrupt the entire ocean food web and weaken a critical climate regulation system.
takeaways: Phytoplankton produce approximately 50 percent of Earth's oxygen
Zooplankton form the critical link between photosynthesizers and fish
Global phytoplankton populations have declined an estimated 40 percent since 1950

faq.question: Why are plankton so important for the global climate?
faq.answer: Phytoplankton absorb CO2 through photosynthesis like terrestrial plants. When they die and sink, they transport carbon to the deep ocean. This biological pump removes billions of tons of carbon from the atmosphere annually, helping regulate global temperatures.

faq.question: What would happen if plankton disappeared?
faq.answer: Virtually all marine food webs would collapse, eliminating fish, whales, and seabirds. Atmospheric oxygen would slowly decline and CO2 levels would rise. It would be among the most catastrophic ecological disasters imaginable, affecting every living thing.
